questions.q: What kind of culture does the book say keeps a company strong?
a: One where people can exchange opinions and point out faults
One where leaders avoid risk and protect the status quo
One focused mainly on beating rivals on price
One where decisions stay with a small group at the top
questions.why: The first lesson says a workplace where people share views and call out mistakes is essential to lasting success.

questions.q: What brought GE close to collapse during the 2008 crisis?
a: A finance arm that took on risky credit and bonds
A failed line of household appliances
A long strike by its manufacturing workers
A botched merger with a European rival
questions.why: The summary describes GE building a bank-like branch that lent risky credit, issued bonds and created a bubble that burst in 2008.

questions.q: What did Boeing do while racing Airbus on the 737 MAX?
a: It skipped pilot training on new features and hundreds died
It slowed production to add extra safety testing
It raised prices instead of cutting engineering corners
It shared its designs openly with regulators
questions.why: The second lesson says Boeing failed to train or even inform pilots about new features, leading to two crashes in 2019.

questions.q: Which cost cuts does the summary warn against?
a: Removing quality control and safety steps to hit targets
Trimming overhead that no longer serves the business
Renegotiating supplier contracts every year
Closing offices that duplicate each other's work
questions.why: The third lesson says Boeing's cuts to manufacturing steps and quality control managers began its downfall.

questions.q: According to the summary, what is profit a result of?
a: Cutting costs or increasing sales
Raising prices faster than competitors
Reducing wages and employee benefits
Postponing investment in new products
questions.why: The third lesson states plainly that profit results from cutting costs or increasing sales.
